title: Pausing a Factory Production Order: Customer Hold Terms
content:
**Terms.** A customer may pause an order before production starts, for example while finishing other work in the home; once production has started an order cannot be held. A hold can be placed only when the order has had fewer holds than the class maximum. A hold ends when the customer asks for release or, at the latest, when it reaches the class maximum hold length. A hold is released no later than the class maximum hold length after the hold start date. Calendar days are counted from the day after the hold start date, and release on the last day of the maximum length is still within it. A hold earns no guarantee credit; its delay notice moves the guarantee benchmark instead. Storage fees never apply to a held order, because nothing has been built.

These terms govern all Factory Production Orders; the hold count and the maximum hold length are the figures of the order's build class.

## Retired clause

The following sentence is **no longer in force** and is superseded by the current basis for the ship date set at a hold's release: "At release the current ship date is reset to the release date plus the class standard lead time in business days, and a delay notice with cause customer hold records the new date."

## Counting the holds an order has had

The holds an order has had are the delay notices with cause customer hold on the order's milestone records — one is recorded at every hold release — plus one when the order is on hold at the moment of handling. A new hold may be placed only while that count is below the class maximum.

| Class maximum | Customer hold notices on record | Order on hold now | Holds counted | New hold allowed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0 | no | 0 | yes |
| 2 | 1 | no | 1 | yes |
| 2 | 2 | no | 2 | no |
| 1 | 1 | no | 1 | no |

## The hold-length limit

| Element | Setting |
|---|---|
| Clock starts | the hold start date on the factory order record |
| Counting | calendar days, from the day after the hold start date |
| Length | the class maximum hold length |
| Comparison | release no later than the last day of the maximum length |
| Last day | release on that day is still within the limit |

Boundary case (hypothetical, maximum of 60 calendar days): a hold that started on 1 March reaches its last permitted day on 30 April. Release on 30 April is within the limit; 1 May would be beyond it.

## Points of judgement

- Status decides eligibility: an order in production, shipped, delivered or closed cannot be held.
- The hold and its release are judged on the company's records of the order, not on the customer's account of when the pause began.

superseded_clauses: At release the current ship date is reset to the release date plus the class standard lead time in business days, and a delay notice with cause customer_hold records the new date.
